title: Advanced
summary: Phrasal verbs that make your English sound natural and fluent.

lessons.meaning: to think of an idea, plan or answer
lessons.note: Three-word verb, not separable: come up with an idea.
examples: She came up with a brilliant idea.
Can you come up with a better name?
We need to come up with a plan by Friday.
reallife: Brainstorming: Let's come up with five ideas for the campaign.
Problem-solving: He came up with a quick fix.

mistakes.right: She came up with an idea.
mistakes.why: Keep all three words: come up with.

dialogue: A: We need a name for our team.
B: Let me think. I will come up with something.
A: Great. Tell me tomorrow.
conversation.task: Say what you would like to come up with a solution for.

lessons.cloze: Can you ___ a good excuse for being late?

options: think of
visit
meet by chance
assessment.why: Come up with = think of an idea.

assessment.prompt: She ___ a great solution. (come up with; past)
assessment.why: Past of come is came.

options: He came up with a plan.
He came up a plan with.
He came with up a plan.
assessment.why: Keep the three words together.

options: invent
avoid
refuse
assessment.why: To invent or create an idea.

senses.meaning: to think of an idea, plan or answer
senses.example: She came up with a brilliant idea.

lessons.meaning: to do something wrong and not be punished or caught
lessons.note: Three-word verb, not separable: get away with it.
examples: He got away with cheating.
You will not get away with this!
She got away with a small fine.
reallife: News: The thieves got away with thousands of rupees.
At school: He thinks he can get away with not doing homework.

mistakes.why: Keep with after get away.

B: And nobody said anything.
A: He always gets away with it.

options: avoid punishment
escape by running
get a present

assessment.why: Past of get is got.

options: You can't get away with that.
You can't get with away that.
You can't get away that with.
assessment.why: Keep the three words together.

options: to win a prize
to avoid being caught
to do wrong without a penalty
assessment.why: Get away with is about avoiding consequences.

senses.meaning: to do something wrong and not be punished or caught
senses.example: He got away with cheating.

lessons.meaning: to think that you are better than someone

options: think you are better than
admire
look at the ground

give up
carry on

options: Don't look down on anyone.

Don't look anyone down on.

senses.meaning: to think that you are better than someone
senses.example: Never look down on people because they are poor.

senses.meaning: to stay at the same level or speed as someone or something

lessons.meaning: to finally find time to do something you have been delaying
lessons.note: Three-word verb, followed by -ing or a noun: get around to cleaning.

Work: Sorry for the delay. I have only just got around to your message.

B: Not yet. I have not got around to it.

travel around
avoid doing
assessment.why: Get around to = finally find time to do.

I'll get around to clean soon.
I'll get around cleaning to soon.

assessment.prompt: Which sentence suggests a long delay?

I did it at once.

assessment.why: Only just got around to = after a long time.

senses.meaning: to finally find time to do something you have been delaying
senses.example: I finally got around to writing the email.

lessons.meaning: to decide not to do something you agreed to do

lessons.meaning: to complete what you started or promised to do

walk behind someone
stop halfway

look after

senses.meaning: to complete what you started or promised to do

senses.meaning: to cause something to happen, especially a change
